History of Present Illness:
38-year-old woman. Thirty hours of focal right lower abdominal pain and nausea. No vaginal symptoms or urinary complaints.

Physical Examination:
Right lower-quadrant tenderness without generalized guarding. Temperature 38.3 C; heart rate 94/min; BP 134/78 mmHg; respiratory rate 22/min; SpO2 98% on room air.

Laboratory Tests:
WBC: 12.9 10^9/L (reference 4.0-11.0)
Hemoglobin: 13.9 g/dL (reference 12.0-17.5)
Platelets: 297 10^9/L (reference 150-400)
Sodium: 138 mmol/L (reference 135-145)
Potassium: 4.1 mmol/L (reference 3.5-5.0)
Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL (reference 0.6-1.3)
CRP: 144 mg/L (reference <5)
Lipase: 43 U/L (reference 13-60)
ALT: 33 U/L (reference 7-45)
AST: 28 U/L (reference 10-40)
Alkaline phosphatase: 107 U/L (reference 40-130)
Total bilirubin: 0.7 mg/dL (reference 0.2-1.2)
Serum pregnancy test: negative (reference negative)

Imaging Findings:
CT abdomen/pelvis: cecal diverticulum with adjacent focal colonic wall thickening and surrounding fat stranding. Appendix is normal; no abscess.
